chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying regarding the domesticated birds of Makkah, which are not the doves of the Sanctuary: 'Whoever slaughters a bird from them while he is not in Ihram, then upon him is that he gives in charity an amount superior to its price. And if he was in Ihram, then a sheep for each bird.'

key_terms.حَمَامِ الْحَرَمِ: Doves of the Sanctuary (specifically those not considered wild game)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a bird in Makkah while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the specific expiation for hunting the domesticated birds of Mecca, distinguishing between the general public and those in Ihram. For non-pilgrims, the penalty is charity exceeding the bird's value, reflecting a compensatory principle, while pilgrims must offer a sheep per bird, aligning with the stricter sacrificial norms of the Hajj rituals.
